docs.title: Coder reference: conventions to watch for
docs.author: HIM Coding Supervisor
docs.body:
While you code these statements, look for these conventions in the Tabular List:
- Combination codes: one code that describes two conditions, or a condition and its complication.
- "Use additional code" and "Code first" notes, including etiology/manifestation pairs.
- Excludes1 and Excludes2 notes.
- "With": the classification presumes a causal relationship between two conditions linked by "with" in the Index (for example, hypertension and CKD) unless the provider says they are unrelated.
- NEC (not elsewhere classifiable) and NOS (not otherwise specified).
- Laterality, and codes that need more characters before they are billable.

docs.title: Coder reference: ICD-10-PCS root operations used in this set
docs.author: HIM Coding Supervisor
docs.body:
Excision: cutting out or off, without replacement, a portion of a body part.
Resection: cutting out or off, without replacement, all of a body part.
Extirpation: taking or cutting out solid matter from a body part.
Drainage: taking or letting out fluids and/or gases from a body part.
Replacement: putting in or on biological or synthetic material that physically takes the place and/or function of all or a portion of a body part.
Insertion: putting in a nonbiological appliance that monitors, assists, performs or prevents a physiological function but does not physically take the place of a body part.
Reposition: moving to its normal location, or other suitable location, all or a portion of a body part.
Section 1 Obstetrics, root operation Extraction: pulling or stripping out or off all or a portion of a body part by the use of force.
Section 5 Performance: completely taking over a physiological function by extracorporeal means.
Section 3 Administration, Transfusion: putting in blood or blood products.

docs.title: Operative Report
docs.author: K. Brandt, MD
docs.body:
Preoperative diagnosis: Acute calculous cholecystitis.
Postoperative diagnosis: Acute gangrenous calculous cholecystitis.
Procedure: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy converted to open cholecystectomy.
Description: Four laparoscopic ports placed. The gallbladder was distended and gangrenous with dense inflammatory adhesions to the duodenum; Calot's triangle could not be safely defined. The procedure was converted to open through a right subcostal incision. The gallbladder was dissected from the liver bed and removed completely; the cystic duct and artery were ligated. A 19 Fr closed-suction drain was left in the gallbladder fossa (peritoneal cavity) and brought out through a separate stab incision.
Findings: Gangrenous gallbladder with multiple stones. No common duct stones.
EBL 150 mL. Specimen: gallbladder with stones to pathology.
